A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Content can be matched reliably across pagination changes and relocated definitions.

before.justification: V3 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR-10, SVHN, and a custom road dataset, including robustness accuracies, curvature analyses, and feature visualizations.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds higher-noise evaluation results and a loss-component ablation study.

M1.justification: The losses in Equations (7)–(13), class-wise noisy-feature alignment, and partial-momentum centroid strategy remain unchanged. Added forward-pass descriptions and disclosed loss weights document the existing procedure; ablation variants do not revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: The datasets and classification tasks remain unchanged. Tables 1–3 extend Gaussian-noise test conditions: maximum standard deviations increase from 16/255 to 20/255 for CIFAR-10, 36/255 to 42/255 for SVHN, and 40/255 to 60/255 for road images.

E2.justification: Figure 1(b) replaces the displayed 'training with noisy data' comparison with 'training with both clean and noisy data' and different t-SNE plots. Tables 1–4 retain the same four baselines: normal training, noisy-only training, mixed clean/noisy training, and stability training.

E3.justification: Section 7.6 introduces an ablation design restricted to clean-data constraints, varying compactness and separability weights and testing regularization weights of 0, 0.001, and 1. Gaussian-noise evaluation grids also expand. Existing splits, training budgets, and Appendix H training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 contains curvature and representation analyses but no empirical component ablation. V4 adds Section 7.6 and Table 5 directly testing the complementary contributions of compactness and separability and the effect of regularization. This substantially expands validation of the loss design, alongside additional higher-noise robustness checks.

E5.justification: Both versions report noisy-test means and standard deviations over 10 independent perturbations with trained models fixed, as clarified in Appendix H. The added noise columns follow this practice. Table 5 supplies point estimates without introducing additional uncertainty estimation or training-seed reporting.

E6.justification: Existing entries in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. New highest-noise accuracies for the proposed method are 89.42±0.11, 90.86±0.08, and 93.65±0.49 on CIFAR-10, SVHN, and road images. Table 5 adds component and regularization results, supporting joint constraints. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v3.

T1.justification: Section 6.1 explicitly restricts the approximation following Equation (16) to a regime where the instability term is sufficiently large relative to the neglected gradient term, refining the mathematical argument. The theorem statements and appendix proofs otherwise remain unchanged; KL/JSD definitions merely move to Appendix G.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same substantive text, and the main contribution claims remain unchanged: discriminative feature constraints, class-wise alignment, the noise–curvature connection, and robustness while preserving clean-data performance. New experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations of robustness beyond training noise levels and a semantic-distortion qualification for stronger noise. It explains the ablation findings and qualifies the curvature argument and the architecture-independent intermediate-layer bound in Remarks 6.1 and 6.3.

D1.justification: V4 discloses default weights alpha=beta=1 and gamma_reg=0.001, two forward passes, and end-to-end training without frozen layers. It replaces the anonymized code pointer with a named GitHub repository. Appendix H, including the already-disclosed 128-dimensional head and training recipes, is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands comparisons with Tang (2013) and Elsayed et al. (2018), emphasizing retained softmax classification, centroid-based margins, and compactness constraints. Some references, including Jin et al. (2019), are removed. The central research positioning remains stable; publication-metadata updates do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized expansions to related work, method explanations, and theoretical discussion, adds Section 7.6, and relocates KL/JSD definitions to Appendix G. Author/contact information and notation are updated, while most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds the parameter-scaling illustration in Figure 5 and the ablation Table 5, replaces Figure 1(b), and adds noise columns to Tables 1–3. Publication headers and content reflow alter layout. Other experimental figure images are retained despite renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: V4 adds useful empirical support for the loss design through Table 5 and extends robustness evaluation in Tables 1–3. Clearer theoretical qualifications and implementation disclosures improve interpretability and reproducibility. The gains are limited: the ablation covers only clean-data constraints and provides no uncertainty estimates, while the core method and existing evidence remain unchanged.
